answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may post offers or vote on reputation updates. When a trade settles, both parties attest to the same receipt; a randomly selected auditor can challenge inconsistent claims, and proven fraud burns the poster’s deposit. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: every fake identity needs its own capital, while splitting one stake across accounts does not multiply voting weight. A bridge may carry receipts from a wharf market, but each still advances the same settlement pulse before funds unlock.
